controller_actions.task: Write module.py exposing solve(data) per the user contract. Process data['ops'] in order without mutating input. Maintain balance and a dict of active holds (id->amount); held = sum of holds; available = balance - held. Per-op check order: (1) kind must be in credit/debit/hold/release else ValueError; (2) for credit/debit/hold, amount must be int (not bool) and >=1 else ValueError; (3) hold: id must not already be an active hold; release: id must be an active hold, else ValueError; (4) debit/hold: amount must not exceed available else ValueError. credit adds to balance; debit subtracts; hold adds hold; release removes hold and ignores any amount. Return {'balance':int,'held':int,'available':int}. Empty ops returns zeros. Standard library only, no I/O.

Write test_cases.json: a JSON list of at least 8 distinct cases, each with 'input' ({"ops": [...]}) and exactly one of 'output' or 'error' (exception class name, e.g. ValueError). Expectations must match the user contract: kinds credit/debit/hold/release; check order (1) kind, (2) amount int>=1 not bool for credit/debit/hold, (3) hold id must be new / release id must be active, (4) debit/hold amount <= available; release ignores amount; result {balance,held,available} with available=balance-held; empty ops returns zeros. Include cases: empty ops; credit then debit; credit then hold; hold then release (with ignored amount); unknown kind error; bool amount error; zero amount error; duplicate hold id error; release unknown id error; debit exceeding available (due to hold) error; hold exceeding available error; invalid amount on an op with a bad id (amount error precedence is not tested ambiguously, keep it consistent with order).
